lead.text: *The book, in one document. Not a substitute for the book — a map to it.*

blocks.text: 1. Two seconds of pause is worth two hours of damage control.
2. Inhale 4, exhale 6 — four times. Physiology, not willpower.
3. Name what you feel. Precision of language → precision of action.
4. One 90-minute deep-work block per day. Phone in another room.
5. Morning sunlight within 30 minutes of waking. Cheapest health lever.
6. Design habits for your worst self. The 2-minute version always.
7. Never miss twice. One miss is nothing; two is a new habit.
8. Procrastination is an emotion, not a discipline problem. Name the flavor.

entries.title: Level 2 — Think Like a Sharp Person

blocks.text: 9. A problem well-defined is half-solved. Slow down before solving.
10. Tag every claim F/S/I/O. Fact, Story, Inference, Opinion.
11. Ask 'how do we know that?' — calmly, of any consequential claim.
12. For every bias, memorize its counter-question. Use before deciding.
13. One real question per meeting. Then seven seconds of silence.
14. First principles: what MUST be true? Then reason upward.
15. Change your mind in public with 'In light of X, I've updated.' Reputation compounds.
16. 30/45/15 sprint. Understand, practice, teach. Then stop.
17. Three sources minimum. Documentation, tutorial, expert reflection.
18. Four-line ask: context, tried, specific request, out.
19. CODA-R: Calm, Observe, Define, Alternatives, Rank, Act, Adapt.
20. When stuck, move. Physical movement often unblocks mental loops.
21. Enough is a decision, not a discovery.
22. LMR: Listen, Mirror (3–5 words), Reflect (one sentence).
23. Point, Reason, Example, Point. Under pressure, PREP saves you.
24. The hard conversation today is cheaper than the same one next month.
25. SBI-I: Situation, Behavior, Impact, Inquiry into intent.
26. Five-column prep before negotiation. Silence after your ask.
27. Watch the eyes in the room. They reveal informal power.
28. Sunday 30. Top Three. Book them into blocks. Defend them.
29. Checklists prevent the errors of cognitive overload. Build them retrospectively.
30. Five-part delegation + reverse brief + written confirmation.
31. Map, measure, move one step. Never redesign the whole process at once.
32. Pre-mortem every project. Write the failure story before starting.
33. The 3-use rule: do it, note it, systemize it.
34. CGCEO-V prompt: Context, Goal, Constraints, Examples, Output, Verification.
35. Verify every AI-generated citation, number, and current-state claim.
36. Three-tab workbook: Raw, Logic, Output. Anyone can inherit it.
37. Six questions before believing a chart. Read the axis first.
38. Password manager + 2FA + passkeys + updates + backups + verify-before-clicking.
39. When phished, own it in the first sentence and change the protocol.
40. Decision 7. In writing. Slept on. Then decide.
41. Reversible decisions: fast. Irreversible: slow. Match effort to door.
42. Give three-point estimates (best, expected, worst). Round to 10%.
43. Judge decisions by process; outcomes by decision quality. Never confuse.
44. Pre-mortem before commit; red-team the plan honestly.
45. Decision journal. Quarterly review. Calibrate honestly.
46. Knowledge is knowing what. Wisdom is knowing what matters.
47. Your calendar and your bank statement are your values.
48. One virtue per month. Small daily action. Nightly review.
49. Meaning is generated by attention, not delivered by achievement.
50. Four ethical lenses: consequences, rules, character, fairness. Use all four.
Print this. Fold it. Keep it. When something in your week goes badly, look at the list and ask: which of these did I not use, and why not?
REMEMBER THIS
*“Fifty shortcuts. Not fifty rules. A menu you select from, depending on the situation.”*
